problem_text: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

ranking.title: Alignment-adaptive residual CDF: weighting the positional correction by measured anatomy alignment

Novelty.review: CDF normalisation on held-out normal scores exists in anomaly-detection libraries and positional normality is used in atlas-based brain methods; weighting a positional correction by an alignment statistic measured on the few-shot supports is new.

Feasibility.review: Inference-only, a few array operations, no training.

Clarity.review: Alignment statistic, residual and reference construction are specified.

Impact.review: Gives an inductive, anatomy-aware normaliser that is safe on unaligned modalities — the deployability property the problem targets.

Validity.review: Sound fallback logic; small-K bias of the residual references remains (addressed by the exact leave-one-out variant).

ranking.title: Content-conditioned expected-normal-score regression
ranking.family: Learned or analytic scale from source modalities

Novelty.review: Predicting the expected normal score of a patch from its content is related to Patch2Loc's learned normal expectations, but using a source-trained regressor to normalise MVFA's branch scores on an unseen modality is new.

Feasibility.review: A small MLP per branch and level trained on source normal patches; cheap.

Clarity.review: Regressor, re-centring and baselines are specified.

Impact.review: Works on aligned and unaligned modalities alike; addresses the anatomy-offset problem generally.

Validity.review: Re-centring with supports handles the shift of the regressor's output to the unseen modality; transfer of the content-to-offset mapping remains the main assumption.

ranking.title: Extreme-value tail extension of the support CDF

Novelty.review: Extreme-value normalisation of anomaly scores is known (patent on EVT score normalisation; EVT score adaptation in inspection); applying a GPD tail to fix ceiling ties of empirical-CDF normalisation under max pooling is a specific, new observation.

Feasibility.review: A GPD fit per branch and level; trivial cost.

Clarity.review: Threshold, fit and diagnostics are fully specified.

Validity.review: Peaks-over-threshold theory justifies the tail model; thousands of support patches make the fit stable.

Novelty.review: Location-scale separation with a positional location and a global CDF scale is a sensible design not found in the medical few-shot anomaly-detection literature.

Impact.review: Useful on aligned modalities; no fallback for unaligned ones.

Validity.review: Its residual references include each support in its own positional median, which biases thresholds at small K.

Novelty.review: Very close prior work: a 2026 study calibrates few-shot anomaly thresholds by leave-one-image-out scoring of the target's normal images and analyses distribution-free certification (industrial data); the medical CLIP setting is the main difference.

Clarity.review: Clear quantile rule and validity cells.

Impact.review: Gives a deployable decision rule with a stated bound, which AUROC-only evaluation lacks.

Validity.review: Valid under exchangeability; the prior work shows that certification is hard, which the idea should discuss.

Impact.review: Helps datasets with strongly varying tissue area.
